newsitem.title: USA: Montana small grain crops get beneficial rain.
newsitem.headline: Montana small grain crops get beneficial rain.

text.p: Soil moisture conditions continued to improve for the week ending July 13, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service reported.
Statewide topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 18 percent short, 76 percent adequate and five percent surplus verus 7 percent short or very short the prior week.
The precipitation received last week was very beneficial for the grains but the hay harvest was held up in some areas.

Winter wheat was mostly headed with 61 percent of the crop starting to turn color and one percent ripe. Ninety-seven percent of winter wheat was headed, up from 95 percent the prior week and near the 99 percent average.
Spring wheat was 76 percent headed and five percent turned versus 61 percent headed and one percent turned a week ago.
Barley was 68 percent headed and seven percent turned.
The first cutting of alfalfa is 71 percent harvested ahead of the five-year average of 67 percent complete.
Oats was 73 percent headed, up from 56 percent last week and the 71 percent average.
